records.region: Southern Córdoba and southwestern Santa Fe, Argentina; Laboulaye–Rosales–southern Rufino–Laguna La Picasa corridor.
records.material_pending_reason: Two readable independent originals were used. The province-scale sheet is contextual; the basin study maps the channels, regulating depressions and receiving lake, but leaves substantial selected paths away from its actual channel network unresolved. Further broad source expansion was not undertaken after recording those specific gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The independently studied La Picasa basin provides practical receiving-lake and regulation-lagoon context. Its named basin, mapped managed system and general surface-flow direction are not treated as proof that the entire selected trace is a river called La Picasa, Quinto or Salado.

completion_scope.headward_scope: Laboulaye-side opening located, but no source-supported drain through the full eastern approach.
completion_scope.lake_and_wetland_scope: R2 passage and the La Picasa endpoint are bounded positive observations. R6/R7 local settings are established with unresolved selected interconnections. Regional marsh and basin mapping is not substituted for those links.
completion_scope.managed_passages: The independent research documents constructed canals and seven regulating depressions. The selected route follows neither the full engineered system nor a demonstrated continuous natural channel; no named canal is assigned from proximity.
completion_scope.branch_scope: The pinned selection contains one mainstem FID and no separately selected tributary fragment. Internal part boundaries are preserved and do not by themselves establish named confluences.
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: Western Laguna La Picasa, on the mapped receiving waterbody; no downstream diversion or outlet extension is included.
unresolved_material_connections: Laboulaye opening to the Rosales/R2 approach
Southern R6 loop and later R7 connecting passage
West-side La Picasa approach and southern hook
completion_scope.gap_character: Original regional geography is visible, but it does not supply source-supported hydrological through-links for several substantial selected intervals. This is one material-pending outcome rather than completed naming-scope hold.

records.supported_name_scope: Laguna La Picasa is supported as the receiving lake only. No representative river-system name is assigned while substantial selected inter-depression connections remain unestablished.

scope_limits: No hydronym is established for the chosen headward opening or the full selected river group.
The absence of a mapped through-channel does not prove that a selected depression lacks intermittent drainage or a local name.
Regulation-lagoon numbers R2,R6,R7 are the research study’s labels, not verified formal natural names.
A future supported representative system may retain distinct local reach and lake names; a uniform scalar name is not required.
Exact banks, first named vertices, present lake extent and current operating drainage arrangements are outside the finding.

records.material_pending_reason: Lago Arari is identified as a bounded selected waterbody passage, but no whole-river candidate is established. The western opening, lake-entry approach, chosen northern outlet connection and long coastal continuation remain material source gaps.
records.completion_scope: Two independently identified publications were examined. One supplied only earlier lawful regional prose before a figure availability pause; one complete original supplied bounded lake cartography but not the western and coastal route. The bounded pass ends with concrete missing source correspondence, not completed naming research.

scope_limits: All three selected fragments are mainstem display-stage fragments; no separately selected tributary was found in the supplied selection.
The study’s small location figure supplies a bounded lake observation, while its more detailed drainage study focuses mainly south and east of the selected corridor.

The selected coastal outlet and possible engineered northern connector remain unestablished; discovery-only Canal das Tartarugas and Tartarugas River labels are not substantive evidence or adopted candidates.
The single material-pending status reflects actual missing through-links, rather than an exact-bank, current-flow or operation requirement.
No available naming registry was verified, and no source label is extended beyond its supported component.

records.region: Eastern Côte-Nord, Québec; western tributary corridor approaching the lower Saint-Augustin river setting.
records.material_pending_reason: The CEHQ regional original omits the first headward connection at the northern opening. Farther downstream, the opaque station076201 annotation box covers a material part of the selected river and prevents tracing that through-link. The final visible reach and junction can be recognized at regional scale, but they do not repair either upstream gap. No permitted detailed original or actually read name-bearing prose was available to complete those links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The inspected CEHQ cartography depicts much of the selected unnamed tributary corridor but does not label that tributary. No selected reach or whole-system name is promoted from nearby labels or discovery excerpts.
records.completion_scope: The single selected fragment was compared throughout against the actual retained CEHQ original. Its opening, long southward corridor, eastward elbow, lateral joins, southeastward lower reach and actual receiving-river junction were separately considered. Most of the ordinary regional corridor is depicted, but the chosen opening and an obscured lower through-link remain material gaps.
records.supported_name_scope: The inspected CEHQ cartography depicts much of the selected unnamed tributary corridor but does not label that tributary. No selected reach or whole-system name is promoted from nearby labels or discovery excerpts.

scope_limits: The initial omitted through-link and the annotation-obscured lower connection remain source-material gaps.
Rivière Saint-Augustin Nord-Ouest is only an unverified discovery lead; the source does not label the selected tributary.
No independently established name or selected passage is assigned to small adjacent lakes or feeders.
The final junction is recognized at regional scale only; no exact bank, current shoreline, hydraulic or tidal-boundary claim is made.
Formal registry status remains unverified, and no automatic/product name application is authorized.

records.material_pending_reason: The chosen northeastern opening and the long intervening mountain corridor and joins are not continuously covered by the inspected originals. Upper Homathko, Tatlayoko Lake and the estuarine terminal are supported only within those mapped intervals.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The inspected upper-valley and lake-outlet river reaches and the terminal estuarine river bear Homathko River. Tatlayoko Lake is a distinct named lake traversed by the selection. The northeastern selected opening and the long intervening mountain corridor have not been completely linked by inspected source material, so the candidate is not established for the entire selected system.
records.completion_scope: Two independently issued original maps support the Homathko River candidate, the distinct Tatlayoko Lake passage, and the estuarine terminal in Waddington Harbour at the head of Bute Inlet. The chosen northeastern opening and much of the intermediate mountain corridor remain material correspondence gaps.
records.supported_name_scope: The inspected upper-valley and lake-outlet river reaches and the terminal estuarine river bear Homathko River. Tatlayoko Lake is a distinct named lake traversed by the selection. The northeastern selected opening and the long intervening mountain corridor have not been completely linked by inspected source material, so the candidate is not established for the entire selected system.

scope_limits: Whole-system name correspondence remains incomplete because the actual chosen opening and the intervening mountain through-links have not been independently mapped in the inspected sources.
No opening creek name, complete tributary-junction sequence, or unseen lake/managed/glacial connector is inferred from search snippets or proximity.
The modeled mainstem length is selection metadata, not an official measured length of Homathko River.
No formal naming-registry status, indigenous-name equivalence, Korean form, exact surveyed source, current flow, precise bank geometry or operating condition is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
